title: Infra CI/CD and GPU Build Pipeline
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview

This document describes the CI/CD patterns and build pipeline used to produce, validate, and deploy GPU-optimized images and Terraform IaC modules for Redwood's GPU fleet. It covers the end-to-end flow from source changes to production node deployment, recommended Terraform module usage, networking/security considerations, capacity and autoscaling guidelines, and operational runbooks for common incidents.

Goals
- Produce reproducible, audited GPU AMIs/container images with deterministic Terraform artifacts.
- Ensure deployments are gated by automated tests and integration checks (perf and smoke).
- Minimize disruption to serving by using canaries, blue/green where practical, and capacity buffers.
- Provide clear runbooks for capacity, eviction, and rollback scenarios.

Scope
- CI/CD: GitHub Actions + internal orchestration (runners on dedicated control plane).
- IaC: Terraform modules stored in infra-modules repo (module registry).
- Image builds: Packer/Buildkite -> artifact registry (AMIs and container images).
- Deployment targets: hosted clusters (kubernetes/gke), dedicated GPU pools, and private customer clusters.

Ownership and Contacts
- Primary: infra-engineering (oncall: infra-sre rotation)
- Image builds and kernels: eng-serving-runtime
- IaC module approvals: infra-architecture board
- Emergency contact: pagers via PagerDuty (infra-gpu escalation)

High-level Architecture
1. Developer makes changes to infra-modules or image sources in git.
2. Pull request triggers CI: lint -> unit tests -> static security scan -> TF plan generation (using remote workspace).
3. Image build pipeline (Packer or BuildKit) runs in isolated build account; produces AMI/container image with hash tag and SBOM.
4. Integration stage: deploy image to staging GPU pool with representative perf tests (latency 95th, pct throughput).
5. If integration passes, change is promoted via Terraform apply in controlled rollout (canary then progressive).

Terraform / IaC Module Guidelines
- Module naming: terraform-<area>-<purpose> (e.g., terraform-gpu-nodegroup, terraform-gpu-ami-builder).
- Versioning: semantic versions; require changelog in module repo.
- Remote state: S3 bucket with DynamoDB locking (AWS) and cross-account state encryption using KMS.
- Workspaces: each environment (dev/staging/prod) uses a dedicated workspace.
- Security: modules must accept iam_roles and security_group_ids as inputs instead of creating defaults.

Recommended module inputs (example):
| input | type | description | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| instance_type | string | GPU instance type | p4d.24xlarge |
| ami_id | string | AMI produced by image pipeline | ami-0abc1234 |
| desired_capacity | number | target nodes in nodegroup | 10 |

CI/CD Pipeline Steps (detailed)
1) PR checks (fast)
   - terraform fmt and validate
   - go/python/unit tests for modules
   - tfsec/snyk security scans
2) Build stage (isolated)
   - Trigger Packer/BuildKit: base image build + runtime libs + CUDA/cuDNN + serving runtime + quant kernels.
   - Generate SBOM and sign image artifact.
3) Integration tests (staging)
   - Deploy to ephemeral staging cluster (use terraform apply with auto-approve=false).
   - Run performance benchmark suite: 95th latency < 250ms for 128-token prompts on target model variant, cold-start < 500ms.
   - Run GPU stress test (mem bandwidth, nvlink tests).
4) Promotion and rollout
   - Tag Terraform module release and image artifact.
   - Apply changes to prod with canary nodegroup (5% of pool). Monitor for 30 minutes.
   - Progressive rollout (25% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated rollback on errors or QoS regressions.

Autoscaling and Capacity Management
- Capacity buffer: maintain a minimum 10% spare capacity across all GPU pools to handle bursts and node failures.
- Target utilization: 65-75% average GPU utilization (sustained); scale policy triggers at 80% for scale-up and <50% for scale-down.
- Preemptible/spot strategy: prefer spot for low-priority workloads, keep mixed instance pools with on-demand fallback.
- Scaling cooldown: 5m for scale-up, 15m for scale-down.

GPU AMI / Image Build Best Practices
- Base image pinned to tested OS kernel + driver combo (list maintained in infra-modules).
- Keep CUDA/cuDNN versions in module variables and compatibility matrix.
- Bake runtime shards and kernel selection configs as part of image build to avoid runtime network fetches.
- Produce both AMI and container images; prefer containerized runtime inside AMI for deterministic launches.
- Include healthcheck endpoint used by orchestration for readiness/liveness (HTTP 200 and /metrics).

Networking and Cloud Accounts
- Separate AWS accounts for build, staging, prod; cross-account IAM roles with least privilege.
- VPC design: isolated subnets for GPU nodes with NAT for egress, restricted ingress (management via bastion/ssh jump/SSM).
- Security groups: only allow serving ports from load balancers and control plane connections on management ports.
- PrivateLink/endpoints for artifact registries and secrets manager to avoid public egress.

Security and Compliance Checks in Pipeline
- Static checks: tfsec, yamllint, container image vulnerability scan (Trivy).
- SBOM produced for each image and stored in artifact registry.
- Signed artifacts: images and Terraform module releases must be signed with infra CI GPG key.
- Audit logs: terraform apply events and image promotions logged to central audit account.

Runbooks and Common Operations
- Node OOM/Crash Loop
  1. Identify affected node via cluster autoscaler events and pod errors.
  2. Drain node (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets).
  3. Capture diagnostics: dmesg, gpu-top, nvidia-smi --query.
  4. If reproducible, mark AMI as deprecated and trigger image pipeline fix.

- Eviction/Spot Loss
  1. Mitigate by shifting priority workloads to on-demand pools.
  2. Use graceful preemption hooks: save KV cache to remote cache and rehydrate on new node.
  3. Rebalance with Terraform if sustained spot loss > 5% of capacity.

- Performance Regression Detected During Rollout
  1. Abort rollout and rollback to previous image tag.
  2. Run perf suite on canary to capture traces.
  3. Open regression ticket and assign to eng-serving-runtime.

Monitoring and Alerts
- Key metrics: GPU_utilization, per-node_p95_latency, node_startup_time, scheduler_pending_time, model_inference_errors.
- Alert thresholds example: GPU_utilization > 90% for 10m (sev2), node_startup_time > 10m for 5 nodes (sev2), rollout_failure_rate > 1% (sev1).

Rollback and Emergency Procedures
- Emergency flag: set "infra/force-rollback" tag in module registry to prevent automatic promotions.
- Quick rollback command (example):
  - terraform workspace select prod && terraform apply -target=module.gpu_nodegroup -var 'ami_id=ami-0previous' -auto-approve
- Postmortem required for any rollback that impacts >1% of traffic or >15m outage.

Cost Controls
- Use recommended instance types and sustained use discounts where applicable.
- Automated reports: weekly cost-per-token by pool and per-model cost attribution.
- CI build artifacts older than 90 days are garbage-collected unless flagged.

Checklist for Module / Image Release
1. PR approved by infra-architecture reviewers.
2. All CI checks passed.
3. SBOM and vulnerability scan negative or addressable.
4. Staging perf verification completed.
5. Module and image signed and tagged.
6. Runbook updated if behavior change detected.

References
- /confluence/eng-infra/terraform-and-iac/infra-iac-and-gpu-fleet-guide-2026
- /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/gpu-capacity-and-infra-runbook-2026
- infra-modules repo (internal): README and module registry

Appendix: Commands
- Terraform plan (example):
  terraform init -backend-config="bucket=redwood-terraform-prod"
  terraform workspace select prod || terraform workspace new prod
  terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars -out=plan.tfplan

- Promote image (example):
  buildkite-agent pipeline upload promote-image.yml --meta image_tag=ami-0abc1234

- Emergency rollback (example):
  aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-prod --launch-configuration-name launch-config-prev
